requirement:
The view of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes` MUST show
each `habeas:coverage` citation attached to the file root or an explicitly
declared function or method. Each entry MUST identify its source item and
source location and show the fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments
supplying its tracked justification under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
When no tracked justification is present, the entry MUST say so.

File-root citations MUST be labelled as file-threshold exception proposals;
function and method citations MUST be labelled as function exception proposals,
following {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions.anchor`.
rationale: The reviewed tests adequately cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.file_map.notes.justifications`. **Obligations and the tests that cover them** - **Show citations on the file root and on explicitly declared functions and methods.** - `notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[notes_show_root_function_and_method_proposals_with_owned_commentary_and_docs]` covers a file root, a free function, an impl method and an unexplained function. It asserts that exactly 1 file-threshold proposal and 3 function proposals appear. - `book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[documentation_includes_non_rust_functions_methods_and_plain_file_roots]` covers Python `def`, TypeScript function and method, and a plain-text file root. It asserts that all four items appear in the combined view. - `notes.rs#mod[tests]/fn[citations_on_modules_and_citation_text_in_literals_do_not_create_explanations]` covers the exclusions. A citation on a module and citation text inside a string literal produce no entry and no "exception proposal". - The nested-module part of the main notes test shows a module citation does not become a file exception. - **Identify the source item and source location.** The main notes test checks the item label (`File root`, `fn[ordinary]`, `impl[Worker]/fn[work]`, `fn[unexplained]`). It checks `Source: code.rs:{first}–{last}` per entry and `First source citation at line N.` per entry. - **Show fenced citation commentary and Rust doc comments.** - The main notes test shows root `//!` docs plus root fenced commentary, function `///` docs plus fenced commentary, and method `/** */` docs plus fenced commentary. - It checks HTML escaping of ``. - It checks that child docs and nested-module commentary do not leak into other entries. - `fn[justification_can_come_from_docs_or_fenced_commentary_but_not_ordinary_comments]` checks docs alone, fenced commentary alone and an ordinary comment alone. It asserts the `Rust doc comments` and `Citation commentary` headings appear where expected. It also asserts an ordinary comment is not shown as justification. - **Say so when no tracked justification is present.** The unexplained function entry shows "No tracked justification is present." and has no "Rust doc comments" section. The ordinary-comment case in the justification test shows the same message. - **Label file-root citations as file-threshold exception proposals and function or method citations as function exception proposals.** The main notes test asserts the exact label counts. The implementation in `notes.rs#fn[entry]` derives the label from whether the item is empty, so one code path serves every language. That makes the Rust-only label assertions sufficient. **Gaps** I found no unacknowledged gaps, and there are no `{fixme}` acknowledgments.

:::{req} check.exceptions.anchor
Habeas MUST provide the built-in `habeas:coverage` under
{cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, with this text:
> Cite this on a source file or explicitly declared function to propose a
> coverage exception. Explain in prose why the item's incomplete execution
> coverage is acceptable. Put the explanation in fenced citation commentary
> or Rust doc comments included in the source item's assessed input. An ordinary
> non-doc comment alone does not supply a tracked justification. The reason
> must be substantive; difficulty alone is not a justification.
> On a file's root item, the exception excuses only
> that file's 80% instrumented-line threshold, including absent measurement
> of its executable code. On an explicit function with a body, it excuses
> that function's recorded zero execution or absence from otherwise usable
> measurement, without excusing the file's threshold.
> The explanation must agree with the current source and any callers or
> configuration assumptions on which it relies. Only a current accepted
> independent assessment permits the exception. A file exception does not
> excuse unexecuted or not-measured functions in that file.
> The citation applies to its source item without conditional build matching
> and may remain when measured coverage satisfies the item's obligations.
Only `{cite}` MAY reference this built-in, inline or fenced using the standard
reference forms of {cite}`requirements.references.roles`. The built-in MUST be
available in every project without a project requirement, site query, or
exception-specific configuration.
